instructions: SECTION 3 · You will hear two students, Maya and Tom, discussing their research project on food waste with their tutor.

groups.instructions: Choose TWO letters, A–E. Which TWO limitations of their research do the students need to discuss?
groups.strategy: Section 3 has three speakers who agree, disagree and change their minds. An option only counts if it is CONFIRMED, not just mentioned.

options.text: the small number of halls studied
the type of students who answered the questionnaire
the time of year the research took place
some waste not being collected in the correct place

questions.explanation: B: replies 'may be the ones who already care about the issue'. D: 'some students didn't use the special bins'. The tutor confirms: 'those are both limitations'. C is raised but rejected — 'the figures were pretty consistent'.

groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

questions.prompt: What did Tom find most surprising?

options.text: Most waste was food that had never been eaten.
Students threw away large amounts of cooked meals.

questions.explanation: 'It was things like bread and fruit that had gone off before anyone ate them.'

questions.prompt: When asked to estimate their waste, students

options.text: guessed about twice the real amount.
guessed about half the real amount.

questions.explanation: 'the average guess was about half of what we actually measured'.

questions.prompt: The tutor recommends showing the comparison between halls over time in
questions.explanation: 'a line graph would be much clearer, because you're showing change over time'.

questions.prompt: Why does the tutor reject a pie chart for food types?

options.text: It would not show change over time.

questions.explanation: Pie charts are 'hard to read with more than five or six categories'; they have nine.

groups.instructions: Who will write each section of the report? Write A for Maya, B for Tom, C for both Maya and Tom.

questions.explanation: Tom: 'I'm going to write the introduction'.
Tutor: 'write the discussion together' and they agree.
Tom: 'I could take those'; the tutor approves.
